papers.title: Exercise modality-specific regulation of sleep stability in mice: An EEG-based comparative study of high-intensity interval training and moderate-intensity continuous training.
papers.summary: This study compared the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and moderate-intensity continuous training (MICT) on sleep stability in mice using EEG. HIIT increased total sleep time and NREM sleep duration, while MICT reduced wake-sleep transitions and prolonged NREM bout duration, suggesting different sleep phenotypes, though no significant differences between the two modalities were found after correction.

papers.title: Chemogenetic manipulation of mPFC neurons counteracts cognitive deficits but leaves sleep disturbances unaffected in a mouse model of chronic intermittent hypoxia.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: This study investigated the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) in cognitive deficits and sleep disturbances induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) in mice. Chemogenetic inhibition of mPFC-IL neurons restored cognitive function and synaptic protein levels but did not improve sleep architecture changes, indicating a dissociation between cognitive and sleep pathologies.

papers.title: Multi-source domain generalization with few-shot calibration for cross-dataset EEG state classification under proxy labels
papers.summary: This preprint presents a reproducible pipeline for aligning eight EEG datasets and evaluates cross-dataset generalization under proxy labels. The benchmark reveals that performance is at chance level due to invalid proxy labels, not transfer method, and provides a transparently reported negative result with an open-source pipeline.

papers.title: TASTE: Trait-like and State-like Two-stream Framework for EEG Imputation.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper introduces TASTE, a two-stream framework for EEG imputation that models trait-like regularities and state-like variations. TASTE improves imputation fidelity and downstream classification performance across five public EEG benchmarks, achieving average MAE/MSE gains of 22.22%/28.60% over strong baselines.

papers.title: Platinum-nanostructured silicon microneedles with scalable fabrication for EEG biosensing.
papers.summary: The study developed and characterized a silicon microneedle electrode array with a streamlined two-step fabrication process, using platinum electrodeposition to create a nanostructured porous surface that increased electroactive area by ~15-fold. In EEG recordings, the nanostructured electrodes achieved higher signal-to-noise ratios than bare microneedles in SSVEP and ASSR paradigms, and eliminated the need for conductive gel compared to conventional wet electrodes.

papers.title: Adaptive Class-wise Multicentric Prototype Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Privacy-Preserving BCIs.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper proposes ACMP-SFDA, an adaptive class-wise multicentric prototype source-free domain adaptation method for EEG-based BCIs. It improves cross-subject classification accuracy while preserving privacy, achieving accuracy improvements of 1.36%, 1.96%, and 1.94% on three datasets compared to state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Intracranial Validation of Magnetoencephalography Across Oscillatory Frequency and Depth
papers.summary: The study validated MEG against concurrent intracranial EEG recordings in epilepsy patients, finding that source-localized MEG accurately estimated oscillatory power and burst dynamics, especially for lower frequencies and superficial sources, and also captured deep hippocampal activity in the theta band. This provides evidence that MEG is sensitive to physiologically meaningful activity in cortical and subcortical regions.

papers.title: Spontaneous changes in the prestimulus alpha power predict both objective and subjective aspects of perception-evidence from 4 paradigms and 471 experimental sessions.
papers.summary: This study analyzed single-trial EEG data from four paradigms (471 sessions) and found that prestimulus alpha power predicts both objective identification accuracy and subjective visibility, contradicting the view that alpha only affects nonspecific cortical excitability. The results support alpha's role in perceptual sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio improvement.

papers.title: Reliability and disease sensitivity are dissociable properties of EEG foundation-model representations
papers.summary: This preprint evaluates nine EEG foundation model representations, finding that test-retest reliability (ICC range 0.08-0.76, CV 53.0%) varies dramatically across models while disease discrimination (AUC CV 5.4%) is relatively stable, indicating these properties are dissociable and not predictable from conventional model descriptors. Alpha-band information contributes disproportionately to reliability, while theta-band information is most important for Alzheimer's and frontotemporal dementia discrimination.

papers.title: Neural and behavioural manifold dynamics align across interacting individuals
papers.summary: Using dual-EEG recordings from 44 dyads and movement-informed deep contrastive learning, the authors found low-dimensional neural manifolds that align across interacting individuals and mirror coordinated behavior. These manifolds show flexible attractor-like organization co-regulated between partners, suggesting interpersonal coordination emerges through intermittent updating of internal dynamics by partner movements.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study used normative modeling of EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients versus controls. More negative frontal complexity deviations were associated with higher pain intensity, even after adjusting for confounders, suggesting a potential marker for pain severity.

papers.title: Topographic gradients of resting-state EEG alpha asymmetry: Network-specific lateralization and age-related dedifferentiation in healthy adults.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: This study recorded resting-state EEG from 160 healthy adults and found a strong anterior-posterior gradient in alpha asymmetry, with minimal prefrontal asymmetry increasing to leftward dominance in central-parietal and posterior temporal sites. Age negatively predicted asymmetry magnitude (β = -0.003, p = .028), but no significant sex differences were found.

papers.title: Dynamic Entropic Mapping of Alzheimer's Neuropathology: Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed EEG Biomarkers through Wavelet Entropy Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used dual-state wavelet entropy analysis of EEG in 30 Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients and 30 controls, finding reduced alpha entropy differences between eyes-closed and eyes-open states in AD. The delta entropy difference in the alpha band correlated strongly with MMSE scores (r=0.9000), suggesting it as a noninvasive biomarker for early AD detection.

papers.title: Daily Bowel Movements are Associated with Stronger Gut-Brain Phase-Amplitude Coupling and Better Cognitive Performance
papers.summary: This study investigated the association between bowel movement frequency and gut-brain coupling in women by recording EEG and EGG. They found that women with daily bowel movements had stronger gut-brain phase-amplitude coupling and made fewer cognitive errors, with a path analysis suggesting faecal short-chain fatty acids mediate this coupling.

papers.title: Right posterior theta during encoding predicts memory performance in virtual navigation.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology
papers.summary: This study recorded EEG from 27 healthy subjects performing a virtual Linear Track Memory task and found that right posterior theta (RPT) power peaked 170-300 ms after cue onset, was increased for reward cues during encoding, and predicted memory performance (d' and β) during recall. The results support RPT's role in encoding salient information for spatial navigation.

papers.title: Personalized adaptive virtual reality experience driven by electroencephalography-based pain recognition.
papers.summary: This study developed a real-time closed-loop EEG-driven VR therapy system that classifies pain levels from brain signals and delivers avatar-guided therapeutic responses, achieving 97.89% accuracy with LightGBM across 11 pain classes. The system demonstrates technical feasibility for scalable, drug-free pain management.

papers.title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network of the P3 including retrosplenial cortex and hippocampus
papers.summary: The study combined MEG and EEG to investigate sources of the event-related P3 component, extending source space to include the hippocampus. Source analysis identified strong sources in retrosplenial cortex and weaker hippocampal sources, with subsequent activity in insula and anterior mid-cingulate cortex, supporting a limbic source network for the P3.

papers.title: Intelligible distracting speech disrupts early auditory attention
papers.summary: The study examined how masker intelligibility affects auditory attention while controlling acoustic similarity and limiting energetic masking, using behavioral and EEG measures. Intelligible maskers impaired performance and reduced target-evoked neural responses compared to scrambled maskers, implicating early sensory filtering.

papers.title: Fourier Evaluation of Tracings and Acidosis in Labor (FETAL) Framework: An In-Silico Evaluation of a Spectral-Divergence Method.
papers.summary: The FETAL framework uses spectral-divergence analysis of fetal heart-rate signals to detect fetal acidemia. Monte Carlo simulations showed that the spectral-divergence score detected graded within-band spectral shifts with high AUROC (0.917 for strong shifts), outperforming traditional scalar metrics, and remained robust under artifact stress (AUROC 0.714).

papers.title: EEG Microstate Sequences as Potential Brain-Computer Interface Triggers Derived from Motor Imagery Classification
papers.summary: The authors used an LSTM-based autoencoder and dense neural network to classify left- and right-hand motor imagery from EEG microstate sequences, achieving peak classification accuracies around 89% with transfer learning. They found that approximately 400 seconds of calibration data are needed to reach 80% accuracy, suggesting microstate trajectories are promising for BCI triggers.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity in Young Adults With Clinically Diagnosed Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Self-Reported Habitual Short Sleep: An Alpha-Band Network Analysis.
papers.summary: The study compared resting-state EEG functional connectivity between young adults with generalized anxiety disorder and habitual short sleep (GAD+HSS) and healthy controls. Significant group differences were confined to the alpha-band wPLI network, with stronger connectivity, higher global efficiency, and lower path length in the GAD+HSS group.

papers.title: Individual heartbeats track distinct prediction processes during human probabilistic learning
papers.summary: Analyzing electrocardiogram and electroencephalogram recordings from 34 participants in a probabilistic learning task, the study found that single cardiac cycles carry separable signatures of anticipation, orienting, and feedback-based updating. Anticipatory deceleration and rebound acceleration scale with model-derived expectations, while the second heartbeat after feedback tracks signed prediction errors and outcome valence.

papers.title: Brain alignment in deep neural networks emerges early and independently of object classification
papers.summary: The authors tracked deep neural network training and found that brain alignment with human fMRI, EEG, and macaque electrophysiology is largely present at initialization and plateaus within 1-5 epochs, while classification accuracy continues to improve. Lesioning revealed that a kernel's contribution to alignment is uncorrelated with its contribution to classification, suggesting alignment reflects visual environment structure rather than classification solutions.

papers.title: Transcranial Acoustoelectric Brain Imaging with High Spatiotemporal Resolution.
papers.summary: The paper presents a full acoustoelectric brain imaging (ABI) system with a 128-element ultrasound phased array, incorporating algorithms for transcranial phase and amplitude correction validated ex vivo. The system achieved precise source localization (error ≤ 0.8 mm) and high-fidelity waveform reconstruction (correlation > 0.84).

papers.title: Sequential prioritization of expected and unexpected information in visual processing
papers.summary: This EEG study found a biphasic temporal mechanism in visual processing: early enhancement of expected image components followed by later prioritization of unexpected components. This pattern was observed for both identity and superordinate (animal vs. non-animal) processing, supporting Bayesian integration and adaptive updating.

papers.title: Effect of a Tinnitus Sound Therapy Application on Tinnitus Relief.
papers.summary: In a 6-month study of 72 chronic tinnitus patients, smartphone-based sound therapy significantly reduced Tinnitus Handicap Inventory and Beck Depression Inventory scores, as well as self-reported annoyance and stress. EEG showed significant reductions in theta, alpha, and gamma power, while subjective loudness did not change.

papers.title: Morroniside promotes awakening from propofol general anesthesia in gastric cancer surgery by regulating hypothalamic GABAergic neurons.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of gastric cancer, morroniside accelerated recovery of righting reflex after propofol anesthesia without affecting induction, and increased hypothalamic GABAergic neuron calcium signals. Morroniside also modulated EEG power and c-Fos expression, suggesting it promotes awakening via hypothalamic GABAergic neurons.

papers.title: Towards precision psychiatry: initial foundations and future directions.
papers.summary: This Perspective discusses precision psychiatry, which uses biomarkers such as EEG and objective behavioral assessments to align therapeutic development with neural biology dysfunctions. Drawing lessons from oncology, it highlights mechanistic approaches and proof-of-concept examples in postpartum depression and schizophrenia.

papers.title: Neural Value Alignment: Human-AI Collaboration Under Goal-Action Ambiguity.
papers.summary: The paper proposes neural value alignment (NVA) which uses reward prediction error (RPE) and state prediction error (SPE) to achieve human-AI alignment under goal-action ambiguity. EEG recordings showed cortical decodability of RPE and SPE, and simulations demonstrated accelerated alignment with RPE-SPE synergy.

papers.title: Residual cortical responses and network reorganization in inherited retinal degeneration: electrophysiological evidence
papers.summary: In retinitis pigmentosa patients, SSVEP amplitudes were reduced for peripheral stimuli but preserved centrally, while TMS-EEG showed enhanced cortical reactivity at occipital sites. This dissociation suggests homeostatic cortical gain rather than uniform decline, indicating the deafferented cortex retains and strengthens response capacity.

papers.title: Brain-computer interface for upper limb functional recovery post-stroke: a meta-analysis of improvement in upper limb motor function and changes in neurophysiological markers.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of 16 RCTs involving 1761 patients found that BCI-mediated rehabilitation significantly improved upper limb motor function (SMD=0.49), activities of daily living (MBI SMD=0.85), and neurophysiological markers (SMD=0.53) after stroke, with greater benefits in subacute stroke patients. The results support BCI as a promising therapeutic modality for stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: Hippocampal Astrocytes Impact Postnatal Development of Inhibitory Connections, Parvalbumin Levels, Social, and Spatial Navigation Behaviors in a Mouse Model of Fragile X Syndrome.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of Fragile X syndrome, astrocyte-specific Fmr1 knockout led to enhanced spontaneous inhibitory postsynaptic currents in hippocampal pyramidal cells despite reduced GABAergic synapse density, without affecting tonic inhibition. Acute inhibition of GABA transport in astrocytes improved parvalbumin expression, spatial memory, and socialization, implicating astrocytic GABA transport in inhibitory circuit development.

papers.title: Evolving epileptic activity under focal rhythmic Delta activity: insights from simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared simultaneous intracranial and scalp EEG in six patients with intracranial hematoma to assess whether focal rhythmic delta activity (RDA) on scalp EEG reflects intracranial epileptic activity. They found that while focal RDA on scalp EEG appeared in all cases, intracranial RDA appeared earlier, and spikes, electrographic seizures, and high-frequency oscillations were often not detected on scalp EEG, suggesting that focal RDA may indicate growing epileptic activity and a target for antiseizure therapy.

papers.title: Graph convolution neural network channel selection with attention for motor imagery EEG decoding.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a graph neural network framework (KCL + UniEEG-Net) that simultaneously selects informative EEG channels and classifies motor imagery tasks. The method achieves performance comparable to full-channel decoding while using fewer electrodes, and outperforms state-of-the-art models on three datasets.

papers.title: Electroencephalogram Utilization, Epileptiform Findings, and Associated Factors Among Children with Epilepsy in Southwestern Uganda: A 5-Year Retrospective Record Review.
papers.summary: This retrospective record review of 427 children with epilepsy in southwestern Uganda found that only 34.9% had undergone EEG, with epileptiform EEGs in 68.5% of those. Female sex and generalized seizures were independently associated with higher likelihood of epileptiform EEGs, highlighting the need for increased EEG use and training.

papers.title: Altered axonal initial segment development links circuit and Kv7 dysfunction in an Fmr1 knockout rat
papers.summary: The study examined CA1 pyramidal neurons in Fmr1 knockout rats at postnatal days 12-15 and 6-10 weeks, finding early transient deficits in sustained firing, action potential broadening, and synaptic vesicle replenishment that recovered by adulthood. These defects were linked to Kv7 channel dysfunction caused by altered axon initial segment development, making Kv7 channels functionally inert.

papers.title: Methods for improving the vertical resolution of natural gamma ray logs.
papers.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
papers.summary: The study proposed and validated two methods (wavelet transform and five-point deconvolution) to enhance the vertical resolution of natural gamma-ray logs to 0.2 m, improving thin-layer identification in reservoirs. Both methods were effective, with the wavelet transform offering flexibility and deconvolution providing stability.

papers.title: Comprehensive flavor profiling and neural perception of yeast extracts from five yeast sources via sensomics, machine learning, and EEG.
papers.summary: This study compared yeast extracts from five sources using an integrated sensory-chemical-neural framework, identifying 52 key odorants and distinct flavor profiles. Machine learning classification achieved high accuracies (up to 96.8%), and EEG revealed neural perception patterns consistent with sensory evaluation.

papers.title: Pathogenic Genetic Variants, Comorbid Autism and Adaptive Developmental Quotient as Independent Predictors of Intellectual Disability in Children With Global Developmental Delay: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model With Calibrated Risk Estimation.
papers.journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable machine learning model to predict progression to intellectual disability (ID) in children with global developmental delay (GDD), using clinical, neurophysiological, and genetic data. The calibrated logistic regression model achieved an AUC of 0.783, with pathogenic genetic variants, comorbid autism, and EEG epileptiform discharges as independent risk factors, and higher adaptive developmental quotient as protective.

papers.title: Mesoporous-Shell Monolayer Plasmonic Architecture Enables Quantitative and Decision-Guided SERS.
papers.summary: This study introduces a mesoporous-shell monolayer plasmonic architecture for quantitative surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), enabling deterministic hotspots and chemical stabilization. The platform achieves ultrasensitive, reproducible detection of chemotherapeutic drugs in complex matrices, and machine learning-assisted analysis enables accurate concentration prediction, with SERS-guided dose adjustment in a mouse model reducing toxicity without compromising efficacy.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
